en: Then, as Rama stood on the battlefield, weary from fighting and lost in thought, he saw Ravana before him, ready for battle.
The holy sage Agastya, who had come with the gods to watch the battle, went up to Rama and spoke.

first: राम राम महाबाहो शृणु गुह्यं सनातनम्।
en: "Rama, Rama, mighty-armed one, listen to this eternal secret, by which, my child, you will defeat all your enemies in battle.
This is the Aditya Hridaya: holy, the destroyer of all enemies and the bringer of victory. Recite it always. It never fails; it is supreme and auspicious.
It is the most auspicious of all blessings and removes every sin. It calms worry and grief, and it is the best means of a long life.
Worship the Sun, Vivasvan, crowned with rays, as he rises: the maker of light, lord of the worlds, honoured by gods and asuras alike.
He is the self of all the gods, radiant, the source of all rays. With his rays he protects the worlds, the gods and the asuras.

first: एष ब्रह्मा च विष्णुश्च शिवः स्कन्दः प्रजापतिः।
en: He is Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, Skanda and Prajapati; he is great Indra, Kubera the lord of wealth, Time, Yama, Soma and Varuna, lord of the waters.

first: पितरो वसवः साध्या ह्यश्विनौ मरुतो मनुः।
en: He is the ancestors, the Vasus, the Sadhyas, the two Ashvins, the Maruts and Manu; the wind and fire, the life-breath of all beings, the maker of the seasons and the giver of light.

first: आदित्यः सविता सूर्यः खगः पूषा गभस्तिमान्।
en: He is Aditya, Savita and Surya; the one who moves through the sky, Pusha, the rayed one; golden-hued, the shining one, whose seed is gold, the maker of day.
He has green horses and a thousand rays; he rides seven horses and is full of light. He destroys darkness; he is Shambhu, Tvashta, Martanda and Amshuman.
He is Hiranyagarbha, both cool and burning, the maker of light, Ravi; fire is within him; he is the son of Aditi, Shankha, the destroyer of cold.
He is lord of the sky and piercer of darkness, master of the Rig, Yajur and Sama Vedas; he sends heavy rain, he is the friend of the waters, and he moves swiftly along his path across the sky.
He gives heat and is a circle of light; he is death; he is tawny and scorches all. He is the seer, the universe, of great splendour, red, the origin of all that exists.
Lord of the stars, planets and constellations, creator of the universe, brightest of all that shine: salutations to you who take twelve forms through the year.
Salutations to the eastern mountain and to the western mountain, where you rise and set; salutations to the lord of the hosts of light and to the lord of the day.
Salutations again and again to the giver of victory, to the joy that victory brings, to the lord of the green horses; salutations again and again to the thousand-rayed one, to Aditya.

first: नम उग्राय वीराय सारङ्गाय नमो नमः।
en: Salutations to the fierce one, the hero, the swift one; salutations again and again to the one who opens the lotus, to Martanda.
Salutations to the lord of Brahma, Shiva and Vishnu; to Surya, whose brilliance is that of Aditya; to the shining one who consumes all, whose form is fierce.
Salutations to the destroyer of darkness, of cold and of enemies, whose self is boundless; to the destroyer of the ungrateful, to the god who is lord of all lights.
Salutations to the one who glows like molten gold, to the fire, the maker of all; to the destroyer of darkness, to the radiant one, the witness of the world.

first: नाशयत्येष वै भूतं तदेव सृजति प्रभुः।
en: This lord destroys all that exists and creates it again. With his rays he dries, he heats and he sends rain.
Dwelling in all beings, he stays awake while they sleep. He is the fire offering (agnihotra) and also its reward for those who offer it.
He is the Vedas, the sacrifices and the fruit of the sacrifices. Of all the actions done in the worlds, this lord, Ravi, is all.
O Raghava, whoever chants his praise in danger, in hardship, in the wilderness or in fear does not lose heart.
Worship him, the god of gods and lord of the world, with a single mind. Recite this three times and you will win in battle.

first: अस्मिन् क्षणे महाबाहो रावणं त्वं वधिष्यसि।
en: In this very moment, mighty-armed one, you will kill Ravana." Having said this, Agastya went back as he had come.
Hearing this, Rama, full of splendour, was freed from grief. Greatly pleased and self-controlled, he held it in his mind.

first: आदित्यं प्रेक्ष्य जप्त्वा तु परं हर्षमवाप्तवान्।
en: Looking at the Sun and reciting it, he felt the greatest joy. He sipped water three times, purified himself, and, mighty as he was, took up his bow.
Seeing Ravana, he came forward to fight with a glad heart, set with all his strength on killing him.

first: अथ रविरवदन्निरीक्ष्य रामं मुदितमनाः परमं प्रहृष्यमाणः।
en: Then the Sun, standing among the hosts of gods, looked at Rama and, happy and delighted, knowing that the end of the lord of the night-wanderers was near, said: "Hurry!"
